claims.text: The studied nanoparticles are initially solid, equimolar Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu particles.
The initial elemental distribution is globally random while retaining slight short-range chemical order.
Short-range chemical ordering and its associated internal lattice strain govern premelting and melting in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles.
Short-range ordering and internal strain kinetically stabilize localized regions of the nanoparticles.
Localized ordering and strain delay surface premelting relative to a random solid solution.
Localized ordering and strain sharpen the overall melting transition relative to a random solid solution.
The five constituent metals have different bond strengths and mixing enthalpies.
Favorable heteroatomic affinities produce local chemical clusters in multielement nanoparticles.
The favorable heteroatomic clusters generate elastic strain fields.
HEA nanoparticles can possess a strained crystal lattice.
Elastic strain fields hinder surface-atom migration until higher local temperatures are reached.
Ordering-induced stabilization makes nucleation of the liquid phase more cooperative.
More strongly ordered nanoparticles will have a higher premelting onset temperature than near-random nanoparticles.
More strongly ordered nanoparticles will exhibit a steeper melting transition than near-random nanoparticles.
Detailed NMF analysis of STEM-EDX data can reveal local compositional segregation that is not evident in ordinary elemental maps.
The controlled comparison holds composition, particle size, atmosphere, and heating protocol constant while varying local chemical ordering.
Changing post-synthesis cooling rates can produce Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticle samples with different degrees of short-range order.
The proposed mechanism is limited to approximately 10–20 nm equimolar particles under inert atmosphere and comparable heating kinetics.
Significant surface segregation, evaporation, or drastic compositional change may invalidate the proposed mechanism.
Failure to observe a reproducible increase in premelting onset or transition steepness with increasing order and strain would reject the hypothesis.
